This is prime anagrammatic problem, so probably recursive. Check against given base and expected. It’s n^2 check if n-1 to n-2 to n-3 …. up to n-2 elements then n-1 elements and that’s two checks. And if we can’t find even anagrammatic one then say no answer. No edge cases.
</reasoning>

<solution>
```python
def solve(s):
    def is_anagrammatic(sub):
        set_sub = set(sub)
        set_s = set(s)
        return len(set_sub & set_s) == len(sub)

    return sum(
        any(
            (
                0 <= idx < len(s) - len(sub)
                and s[idx:idx + len(sub)] == sub
                and is_anagrammatic(s[idx:idx + len(sub)])
            )
            for idx in range(len(s))
        )
        for sub in set(s)
        if sub.isdigit()
    )
```
</solution>
